category_title: Students in an inclusive urban classroom exhibiting high-frequency disruptive behaviors and low academic engagement
minimal_context: The student is transitioning to independent work at their desk following a mini-reading lesson during reader's workshop.
dialogue:
TUTOR: The mini-reading lesson is finished. Please sit down at your desk and work on your assigned task.

STUDENT: (Stands up and walks away from the desk area, talking loudly to a peer) I'm not doing that right now!

TUTOR: You need to sit down and focus on your reading.

STUDENT: (Pushes past another student in the congested pathway between the desks) Move out of my way!

TUTOR: Please keep your hands to yourself and go to your desk.

STUDENT: (Throws a pencil across the room) This is stupid! I'm not doing this [profanity] work!

options.A: Invite the student to participate in choral reading of a shared text during reader's workshop.
options.B: Represent information in various ways by including movement and physical activity to explore reading concepts.
options.C: Provide individual storage space for the student, such as chair bags or desks with compartments.
options.D: Assign reflective journal entries in which the student is encouraged to write or draw freely.
